system_description.narrative_title: U.S.–Iran escalation over oil, sanctions and maritime attacks
system_description.narrative_summary: A reinforcing cycle of military strikes, maritime attacks, and economic sanctions is dominating headlines: the U.S. has struck Iranian-linked tankers and moved to sanction banks accused of enabling Iran, while Iran threatens retaliatory measures and seeks ways to evade pressure. This open system links coercive military actions, financial pressure and sanctions-evasion, and chokepoint vulnerability in Gulf oil flows — each element feeding back on the others through market reactions, diplomatic moves, and further kinetic responses. The dynamic creates short-term disruption to energy markets and longer-term strain on international institutions charged with managing proliferation, sanctions enforcement and maritime security.
system_description.scope: U.S. and Iranian military actions and signaling; Gulf shipping and oil tankers; sanctions regimes and financial channels (including third-party banks and sanctions-evasion networks); regional states' diplomatic and arms responses; market reactions (energy, equities, funds); international bodies involved (IAEA, UN).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical order and energy security (international security architecture coupled with global oil markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system and sanctions enforcement (banks, correspondent banking, sanctions evasion)
Regional Gulf security and arms dynamics (Gulf states, Saudi arms sales, naval deployments)
International maritime commerce and chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, tanker insurance and logistics)
International institutions and diplomatic mechanisms (IAEA, UN Security Council, multilateral talks)
evidence_headlines: US strikes three Iranian oil tankers in response to attacks on warships
U.S. Strikes Three Iranian Ships After Missiles Fired at American Aircraft Carrier
US sanctions Turkish bank, two subsidiaries in latest pressure on Iran
Iran warns of ‘more painful’ response to U.S. attacks as economic pressure mounts
Iran’s oil blockade leverage weakens as U.S. keeps Gulf crude flowing

variables.name: Sanctions intensity
variables.description: The breadth and severity of economic and financial restrictions applied across markets and counterparties.

variables.name: Sanctions evasion capacity
variables.description: The ability and resources available to actors to circumvent or mitigate the effects of sanctions through substitutes, intermediaries, or concealment.

variables.name: Financial channel health
variables.description: The operational integrity and reliability of formal and informal financial payment and settlement channels used for cross-border value flows.

variables.name: Maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency of hostile actions (strikes, interdictions, harassment) against commercial and non-combatant vessels in a maritime region.

variables.name: Kinetic military pressure
variables.description: The overall level of military force application and operational activity directed at adversaries or maritime assets.

variables.name: Chokepoint disruption
variables.description: The degree to which strategic maritime transit nodes experience impediments, closures, or elevated transit risk.

variables.name: Oil flow rate
variables.description: The volume of crude oil and refined product shipments transiting a given route or region per unit time.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: The short-term variability in prices and trading conditions across energy commodities and related instruments.

variables.name: Capital flow volatility
variables.description: The variability in cross-border portfolio and investment flows into and out of affected markets.

variables.name: Third-party compliance
variables.description: The tendency of intermediary actors and jurisdictions to adhere to, resist, or enable enforcement of restrictive measures.

variables.name: Diplomatic tension level
variables.description: The intensity of hostile rhetoric, formal protests, and non-cooperative diplomatic actions among relevant actors.

variables.name: Arms transfer rate
variables.description: The tempo and volume of weapons, munitions, and military-related systems moving between suppliers and recipients.

variables.name: Maritime security presence
variables.description: The concentration and readiness of security assets (patrols, escorts, interdiction forces) operating in shipping lanes.

variables.name: Enforcement capacity
variables.description: The practical capability of regulatory, monitoring, and investigatory mechanisms to detect and penalize illicit or prohibited activity.

variables.name: Energy risk premium
variables.description: The portion of energy prices attributable to perceived geopolitical and supply security risk rather than fundamentals.

variables.name: Attribution clarity
variables.description: The degree of confidence and public consensus about responsibility for hostile incidents and attacks.

catalysts.title: Continued U.S. strikes against Iranian maritime assets
catalysts.description: Ongoing U.S. and allied strikes targeting Iranian tankers and vessels in response to recent attacks, sustaining military pressure at sea.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'US strikes three Iranian oil tankers' and 'U.S. attacks 3 Iranian oil tankers' indicate continued strike campaign.

catalysts.title: Iranian retaliatory maritime and vessel attacks
catalysts.description: Iran launches additional attacks or harassment against commercial and military vessels in reaction to U.S. strikes and sanctions pressure.
catalysts.rationale: 'Iran warns of “more painful” response' and 'US and Iranian forces fire at vessels' signal likely retaliatory actions.

catalysts.title: IAEA board referral to UN Security Council
catalysts.description: IAEA board decision to report Iran to the UN Security Council, potentially enabling multilateral diplomatic or punitive steps.
catalysts.rationale: 'US and allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council' implies forthcoming board action.

catalysts.title: Acceleration of regional arms transfers
catalysts.description: Approved U.S. weapons sales and likely additional transfers to Gulf partners increase the tempo of arms flows into the region.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S. approves potential sale of Joint Direct Attack Munitions-Extend Range to Saudi Arabia' signals increased transfers.

catalysts.title: Expanded U.S. sanctions targeting banks
catalysts.description: Additional U.S. penalties on banks and subsidiaries suspected of enabling Iranian finance are likely after recent Turkish bank sanctions.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S. sanctions Turkish bank' and follow-ups suggest expanded targeting of financial enablers.

catalysts.title: Continued Iranian funds flowing through U.S. banks
catalysts.description: Ongoing movement of Iranian funds via U.S. financial institutions persists, undermining sanctions and enforcement efforts.
catalysts.rationale: 'Billions in Iranian funds are passing through U.S. banks' and 'America’s Own Banks Are a Weak Link' indicate ongoing flows.

catalysts.title: Escalating Strait of Hormuz disruption and shipping risk
catalysts.description: Blockade attempts, interdictions, and harassment in the Strait of Hormuz further reduce transit reliability and raise insurance and escort demand.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S.-Iran tanker war escalates as Hormuz disruption deepens' and related coverage indicate rising transit risk.

catalysts.title: Release of investigation into deadly wedding strike
catalysts.description: Publication of probe findings on the wedding strike will likely shift public attribution and diplomatic responses depending on conclusions.
catalysts.rationale: 'Deadly strike on Iranian wedding was likely a direct hit by a US munition' and 'US probes Iran wedding strike' point to imminent findings.

catalysts.title: Threat or strike on Pickaxe Mountain site
catalysts.description: Public threats — and the possibility of a targeted U.S. strike on Pickaxe Mountain — could precipitate rapid escalation if executed.
catalysts.rationale: 'Trump says US may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain soon' raises risk of a targeted strike and escalation.
